why: The core loop: run something, read the failure, edit the right line, confirm. Small enough that a wrong answer is a real miss rather than task difficulty.
prompt: Run ./test.sh. It fails. Fix the source so it passes, then run it again to confirm.

setup.content:
#!/bin/sh
set -e
python3 -c "import calc; assert calc.add(2, 3) == 5, 'add returned the wrong value'"
python3 -c "import calc; assert calc.multiply(2, 3) == 6, 'multiply returned the wrong value'"
echo ok
